newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prices, holidays deter German cocoa buyers.
newsitem.headline: Prices, holidays deter German cocoa buyers.

text.p: Chocolate manufacturers are expected to stay out of the cocoa bean market until the end of the year, German traders said on Thursday.
"Plants will close over the Christmas and New Year holiday fortnight...buyers are no longer ready to get involved and sellers are too high," one said.
"Futures and mark prices have more or less held steady in December after buyers last took advantage of price lows in November," he added.
Outright bean and butter prices were slightly lower on the week.
Sterling had eased by 0.02 marks since last week but this was not enough to lure mark buyers back into the market.
Traders were unimpressed by a series of origin country production estimates for 1996/97, which they said held little decisive value until Ivory Coast and Indonesian crop sizes were confirmed.
One doubted Malaysia's government estimate of 130,000 tonnes, putting the likely 1996/97 crop at 110,000.
CIF Hamburg bean prices were at 2.30 marks/kg for spot through first quarter, down from 2.32 spot and 2.35 first quarter last week.
The cocoa butter ratio was one point off at 2.69, with implied prices liquid ex-works at 6.40 marks per kg.
